title: Semantic Model Forge bounded external-research reports

entries.title: Counterexample-Guided Abstraction Refinement

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Primary abstract and bibliographic record used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: Counterexample-Guided Abstraction Refinement Clarke Grumberg Jha Lu Veith

entries.attacked_harness_question: Will SMF repair a candidate only after separating a candidate defect from a spurious, out-of-scope, or auxiliary counterexample?
entries.falsifier: Exhibit a forge run in which an incoherent, out-of-scope, or representation-created counterexample automatically edits the semantic candidate.
entries.bounded_source_report: Clarke et al. present an iterative program-verification method in which an abstract model can admit spurious counterexamples and analyzed counterexamples guide refinement.
limitations: The source concerns formal program abstraction with a concrete model and abstraction relation.
It does not establish soundness or convergence for philosophical semantic repair.

entries.title: Use of Competency Questions in Ontology Engineering: A Survey

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Primary abstract and bibliographic record used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: Use of Competency Questions in Ontology Engineering: A Survey Monfardini Salamon Barcellos

entries.attacked_harness_question: Does every SMF research question retain its scope, model decision, and rationale while remaining explicitly revisable?
entries.falsifier: Find a research-question record whose intended use or model consequence is absent, or whose later revision overwrites rather than preserves its original rationale.
entries.bounded_source_report: Monfardini, Salamon, and Barcellos report a survey of 63 ontology engineers in which competency questions were used chiefly to define scope and evaluate ontology conceptualization, while respondents still reported difficulties writing, using, and managing them.
limitations: The survey reports ontology-engineering practice and perceptions, not semantic sufficiency.
Its sample was limited and primarily academic.

entries.title: Discerning and Characterising Types of Competency Questions for Ontologies

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Versioned primary paper text and abstract used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: Discerning and Characterising Types of Competency Questions for Ontologies

entries.attacked_harness_question: Does SMF type each competency question by purpose so that a scoping question cannot silently become a validation verdict?
entries.falsifier: Find a path in which a scoping, foundational, relationship, or metaproperty question is treated as an automatically answerable validation test without a separate interpretation.
entries.bounded_source_report: Keet and Khan propose a first model distinguishing scoping, validating, foundational, relationship, and metaproperty competency questions, and report an annotated repository of 438 questions.
limitations: This is a 2024 preprint and presents a first model rather than an exhaustive taxonomy.
It does not establish that competency questions settle philosophical semantics.

entries.title: On the Roles of Competency Questions in Ontology Engineering

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Primary publisher abstract and bibliographic record used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: On the Roles of Competency Questions in Ontology Engineering Keet Khan

entries.attacked_harness_question: Does each SMF research question preserve its purpose and motivation rather than treating every question as a request for a fact?
entries.falsifier: Find a research-question record that contains only a query string and has no linked problem, purpose, rival consequence, or intended decision.
entries.bounded_source_report: Keet and Khan argue that competency questions can be complex acts with purposes beyond fact retrieval, including knowledge acquisition, knowledge organization, and validation.
limitations: This is a position paper; its question taxonomy is not a completeness theorem.
The publisher first-online date is 2024, while the proceedings citation is catalogued as 2025.

entries.title: A Survey on Metamorphic Testing

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Primary abstract and bibliographic record used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: A Survey on Metamorphic Testing Segura Fraser Sanchez Ruiz-Cortes

entries.attacked_harness_question: Does every SMF metamorphic test state its transformation, preconditions, and expected relation independently of the observed candidate output?
entries.falsifier: Find a metamorphic test whose expected relation is inferred from the system behavior under test, or whose violation automatically blames the candidate rather than reopening the relation and fixture.
entries.bounded_source_report: Segura et al. survey metamorphic testing as checking a necessary relation across executions produced from related input transformations when an exact expected result for one execution is impractical.
limitations: Metamorphic relation choice is domain-dependent and may itself be defective.
Passing chosen relations is only a partial oracle and does not establish semantic adequacy.

entries.title: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Primary abstract and bibliographic record used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey Barr Harman McMinn Shahbaz Yoo

entries.attacked_harness_question: Can any research provider, language model, test runner, or proof tool issue a final semantic verdict without human adjudication?
entries.falsifier: Exhibit a valid execution path in which a machine result changes human adjudication status or accepts target semantics without an explicit human decision record.
entries.bounded_source_report: Barr et al. define the test-oracle problem and survey specified, derived, implicit, and human-oracle approaches, noting a residual role for human domain judgment when automation is inadequate.
limitations: The survey concerns software testing rather than philosophical or language-model judgment.
Human oracle information is fallible and does not confer certainty.

entries.title: The Counterexample Game: Iterated Conceptual Analysis and Repair in Language Models

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Versioned primary paper text and abstract used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: The Counterexample Game: Iterated Conceptual Analysis and Repair in Language Models

entries.attacked_harness_question: Can definition growth, iteration count, or language-model judge acceptance advance the SMF semantic ratchet without human defect-specific adjudication?
entries.falsifier: Exhibit a forge path in which added clauses, repeated iterations, or model votes cause adoption, or in which an unreviewed generated counterexample automatically triggers repair.
entries.bounded_source_report: Drucker and Mahowald report that extended language-model counterexample-repair chains produced increasingly verbose definitions without improved judged accuracy, while the model judge accepted more counterexamples than experts on a 60-item human-rated subset.
limitations: Human evaluation covered 60 counterexamples, not the complete corpus.
Definition accuracy and concision were rated by a language model, and the concepts were not Popperian epistemology.

entries.title: PROGRESS: Property-Guided Regression Search for Semantic Falsification

primary_inspection.inspected_scope: Versioned primary abstract and bibliographic record used for the bounded source report.

discovery.query: PROGRESS: Property-Guided Regression Search for Semantic Falsification

entries.attacked_harness_question: Can prior candidate behavior or stored regression output define the expected semantic result of an SMF test?
entries.falsifier: Find a replay test that derives its expected outcome from the candidate under test rather than from a separately stated, human-reviewable semantic relation.
entries.bounded_source_report: Mo et al. warn that regression oracles derived from a program under test can preserve existing faults as expected behavior, and propose properties generated from intent-bearing code context while limiting implementation leakage.
limitations: This is a 2026 software-testing preprint, not a semantic-method result.
Its properties are generated from intent-bearing code context and do not supply this project's semantic intent.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Use counterexample triage before deciding whether a candidate, auxiliary, test, or scope should be repaired.
project_use_proposals.rationale: The source offers a useful engineering analogy while its formal verification guarantees do not transfer to philosophical semantics.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Require each research question to retain its scope, intended decision, and rationale.
project_use_proposals.rationale: The reported uses and management difficulties motivate traceability controls without making competency questions semantic authorities.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Type competency questions by purpose so scoping questions cannot silently become validation verdicts.
project_use_proposals.rationale: The proposed taxonomy is useful attack vocabulary but is explicitly treated as non-exhaustive and non-authoritative.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Record the purpose and motivation of each harness question separately from its query text.
project_use_proposals.rationale: Treating questions as purpose-bearing engineering artifacts helps expose hidden decisions without importing the paper's taxonomy into CR-1.0.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Use explicit local transformation relations as fallible semantic test instruments.
project_use_proposals.rationale: Metamorphic relations can expose candidate differences while their selection remains independently criticizable.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Require explicit human escalation when the operative semantic specification remains informal or contested.
project_use_proposals.rationale: The oracle problem motivates a workflow boundary; it does not make human judgment infallible or externally define target semantics.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Treat definition growth and language-model judge acceptance as possible defects rather than improvement evidence.
project_use_proposals.rationale: The contemporary study supplies a bounded warning about its tested repair chains, not a universal result about conceptual analysis.

project_use_proposals.proposed_use: Forbid deriving a semantic test's expected result from the candidate or stored behavior under test.
project_use_proposals.rationale: The source's warning about regression-derived assertions motivates an anti-leakage control without supplying this project's semantic intent.
